purpose: Cimetidine is used to treat heartburn, acid indigestion, and stomach ulcers. It helps relieve the burning feeling in your chest or stomach caused by too much acid. It can also be used to prevent ulcers from coming back.
how_it_works: Your stomach has special spots called H2 receptors that tell it to make acid. Cimetidine blocks those spots, so your stomach makes less acid. With less acid, your heartburn goes away and your ulcer gets a chance to heal.
common_side_effects: Most people do well on this medicine, but some may notice headache, dizziness, or mild diarrhea. Some people feel a little tired or have an upset stomach when they first start taking it. These effects are usually mild and go away on their own.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, since your dose may need to be adjusted. Cimetidine can interact with many other medications — including blood thinners, certain heart medicines, and seizure drugs — so always share your full medication list with your pharmacist or doctor. Avoid taking antacids within 1 hour of this medicine, as they can reduce how well it works. If you notice black or bloody stools or are vomiting blood, seek medical attention right away.
typical_dosing: For heartburn relief, adults typically take 200 mg up to twice a day as needed, or as directed by your doctor. For ulcers, your doctor may prescribe higher doses, often taken once at bedtime or split throughout the day. Always follow the instructions on your label or from your healthcare provider.
